record.original_question: Using the closed-form formula for the boundary of the cycling region of a given cycle length K, the paper plots additional intermediate regions obtained by substituting fractional values of K into that formula, and these regions appear to fill the previously blank parameter region without overlapping the Lyapunov region. Since a notion of cycles of fractional length has not been defined, what mathematical object or dynamical behavior do these intermediate regions represent, and what do they imply about the blank regions?

evidence.quote: Using the closed form formula of the border of each cycling region of a given length K (that we obtained in [Goujaud et al., 2023b, Theorem 3.5]), we displayed in Figure 8 some intermediate regions plugging fractional values of K in the latest formula.
What we observe is that the union of a continuum of those regions seems to perfectly recover the blank regions without overlapping with the green ones, perfectly completing the figure.
Since we did not define the notion of cycles of fractional length, what do those intermediate regions actually represent? What does it say about those blank regions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Polyak's Heavy-Ball method applied to minimizing a strongly convex quadratic function f(x) = (L/2) x^2 with L>0, given by the recursion
  x_{t+1} = x_t - α ∇f(x_t) + β (x_t - x_{t-1}),
parametrized by a step size α>0 and a momentum parameter β∈(-1,1). For each integer K ≥ 2, define the "cycling region" C_K ⊂ R_{>0} × (-1,1) as the set of pairs (αL, β) for which the iterates produced by the method (in the one-dimensional quadratic setting) exhibit a periodic orbit of length exactly K. It is known that the boundary ∂C_K admits a closed-form analytic expression Φ(αL, β, K) = 0 that depends smoothly on the parameter K, so that one may formally substitute non-integer real values K ∈ (2,∞) into Φ to obtain a one-parameter family of curves Γ_K in (αL, β)-space. Let L denote the "Lyapunov region" of parameters for which the method admits a quadratic Lyapunov function ensuring linear convergence, and let B denote the "blank region": the complement, inside the stability region, of L and of the union ⋃_{K∈Z, K≥2} C_K.

Empirically, the union ⋃_{K∈R, K≥2} {Γ_K-bounded region} appears to cover B exactly, without overlapping L.

(a) Give a rigorous mathematical interpretation of the regions defined by Γ_K for non-integer K ≥ 2, in terms of the dynamics of the Heavy-Ball iteration on a one-dimensional quadratic; in particular, identify the dynamical or asymptotic behavior of the iterates (x_t) for parameters lying on Γ_K when K is not an integer.

(b) Using this interpretation, prove or disprove that the blank region B is exactly equal to the union of the curves Γ_K for K ∈ [2, ∞) ∖ Z, and characterize the long-time behavior of the Heavy-Ball iterates for parameters in B.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of two open riddles on Heavy-Ball dynamics in a 2025 open-problem note. No subsequent work resolving the meaning of the fractional-K intermediate regions or characterizing the blank parameter region appears to be available; related literature on Heavy-Ball cycling and Lyapunov regions does not address fractional cycle length.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Two Riddles in Heavy-Ball Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Presents two open problems on Polyak's Heavy-Ball algorithm, including the question of what fractional-length cycling regions represent and what they imply about the blank parameter region.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Provable non-accelerations of the heavy-ball method
status_evidence.snippet: Provides closed-form formulas for the boundaries of cycling regions of integer length K, but does not interpret fractional values of K.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature treats only integer cycle lengths, leaving the fractional-K interpretation unresolved.
